q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT b1.bar, b2.bar FROM serves AS b1 JOIN serves AS b2 ON b1.beer = b2.beer AND b1.bar <> b2.bar WHERE b1.beer IN (SELECT serves.beer FROM serves WHERE serves.bar = b2.bar) AND NOT b2.bar IN (SELECT s2.bar FROM serves AS s2 WHERE NOT s2.beer IN (SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.bar) AND s2.bar = b2.bar)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they are checking for different conditions in the EXISTS clauses. Q1 checks for beers that are served by a bar b1 but not by any other bar, and also checks for beers that are served by a bar b2 but not by b1. Q2, on the other hand, checks for beers that are served by a bar b1 and also by another bar b2, and then checks if b2 serves the same beer that b1 serves and if b2 does not serve any beer that b1 does not serve.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have three bars (b1, b2, b3) and three beers (beer1, beer2, beer3). b1 and b2 serve beer1, but b3 does not serve beer1. b1 serves beer2, but b2 and b3 do not serve beer2. b2 serves beer3, but b1 and b3 do not serve beer3.
